- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when the required content genuinely needs more space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via the sync procedure there; re-apply or retire the logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

</system-reminder>

123	/**
124	 * Resolve the default worker count for one aggregate.
125	 * @param selectedMode - aggregate whose resource posture applies.
126	 * @param total - number of gates in the aggregate.
127	 * @param available - host CPU availability for ordinary modes.
128	 * @returns the default worker count and its diagnostic source.

130	export function defaultConcurrency(
131	  selectedMode: Mode,
132	  total: number,
133	  available = availableParallelism(),
134	): ConcurrencyDefault {
135	  if (selectedMode === 'ci-consumers') return { workers: total, source: 'ci-consumers gate count' }
136	  // Local modes cap workers: several doc gates each build a full ts.Program,
137	  // so an uncapped default on a large host trades wall clock for memory blowups.
138	  const localCap = selectedMode === 'check-all' || selectedMode === 'doc-sync'
139	  const modeLimit = localCap ? Math.min(4, available) : available
140	  return {
141	    workers: Math.min(total, modeLimit),
142	    source: localCap
143	      ? `${available} available CPU(s), ${selectedMode} cap 4`
144	      : `${available} available CPU(s)`,
145	  }
146	}

473	// The heavy suites run uninstrumented beside the thresholded gate: their
474	// compiler- and subprocess-bound fixtures pay a multiple of their runtime
475	// under v8 instrumentation while contributing nothing the thresholds need
476	// (membership rules in scripts/coverage-exempt.ts).
477	//
478	// DSH_COVERAGE_MAX_WORKERS is the lane's worker budget, so the two parallel
479	// gates split it instead of each claiming it whole (the failover pool's
480	// 8 x 6-instance bound assumes one lane never exceeds its value). The exempt
481	// gate's wall clock is dominated by its longest single file, so it takes the
482	// small share. A budget of 1 gives each gate 1 worker; lanes that need a
483	// strict total of one (the serial reference jobs) also set
484	// DSH_GATE_CONCURRENCY=1, which keeps the gates from overlapping at all.
485	function coverageWorkerArgs(): { instrumented: string[]; exempt: string[] } {
486	  const [flag] = positiveIntArg('DSH_COVERAGE_MAX_WORKERS', '--maxWorkers')
487	  if (flag === undefined) return { instrumented: [], exempt: [] }
488	  const total = Number.parseInt(flag.split('=')[1] ?? '', 10)
489	  const exempt = Math.max(1, Math.floor(total / 3))
490	  const instrumented = Math.max(1, total - exempt)
491	  return {
492	    instrumented: [`--maxWorkers=${String(instrumented)}`],
493	    exempt: [`--maxWorkers=${String(exempt)}`],
494	  }
495	}

645	/**
646	 * Reject a gate list whose graph cannot be executed unambiguously.
647	 * @param gates - complete aggregate to validate.
648	 */
649	function validateGateGraph(gates: readonly Gate[]): void {
650	  if (gates.length === 0) throw new Error('run-gates: gate graph has no gates.')
651	
652	  const ids = new Set<string>()
653	  for (const gate of gates) {
654	    if (ids.has(gate.id)) throw new Error(`run-gates: duplicate gate id ${JSON.stringify(gate.id)}.`)
655	    ids.add(gate.id)
656	  }
657	  for (const gate of gates) {
658	    for (const dependency of gate.needs ?? []) {
659	      if (!ids.has(dependency)) {
660	        throw new Error(`run-gates: gate ${JSON.stringify(gate.id)} depends on unknown gate ${JSON.stringify(dependency)}.`)
661	      }
662	    }
663	  }
664	
665	  const cycle = findDependencyCycle(gates)
666	  if (cycle !== undefined) throw new Error(`run-gates: dependency cycle: ${cycle.join(' -> ')}.`)
667	}
668	
669	function findDependencyCycle(gates: readonly Gate[]): string[] | undefined {
670	  const byId = new Map(gates.map(gate => [gate.id, gate]))
671	  const complete = new Set<string>()
672	  const active = new Map<string, number>()
673	  const path: string[] = []
674	
675	  const visit = (id: string): string[] | undefined => {
676	    if (complete.has(id)) return undefined
677	    const cycleStart = active.get(id)
678	    if (cycleStart !== undefined) return [...path.slice(cycleStart), id]
679	    const gate = byId.get(id)
680	    if (gate === undefined) return undefined
681	
682	    active.set(id, path.length)
683	    path.push(id)
684	    for (const dependency of gate.needs ?? []) {
685	      const cycle = visit(dependency)
686	      if (cycle !== undefined) return cycle
687	    }
688	    path.pop()
689	    active.delete(id)
690	    complete.add(id)
691	    return undefined
692	  }
693	
694	  for (const gate of gates) {
695	    const cycle = visit(gate.id)
696	    if (cycle !== undefined) return cycle
697	  }
698	  return undefined
699	}

701	/**
702	 * Validate and run one aggregate before the injected executor can start a child.
703	 * @param gates - complete aggregate to execute.
704	 * @param maxActive - maximum concurrent child count.
705	 * @param execute - child-process executor.
706	 * @param observe - result observer invoked when each gate settles.
707	 * @returns results in aggregate order.
708	 */
709	export async function runGates(
710	  gates: Gate[],
711	  maxActive: number,
712	  execute: GateExecutor,
713	  observe: ResultObserver = () => {},
714	): Promise<GateResult[]> {
715	  validateGateGraph(gates)
716	  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(maxActive) || maxActive < 1) {
717	    throw new Error(`run-gates: max concurrency must be a positive integer, got ${JSON.stringify(maxActive)}.`)
718	  }
719	  const states = new Map<string, GateState>(gates.map(gate => [gate.id, 'pending']))
720	  const results = new Map<string, GateResult>()
721	  const running: RunningGate[] = []
722	
723	  for (;;) {
724	    let madeProgress = false
725	    while (running.length < maxActive) {
726	      const ready = gates.find(gate => states.get(gate.id) === 'pending' && dependenciesPassed(gate, states))
727	      if (ready === undefined) break
728	      states.set(ready.id, 'running')
729	      running.push({ gate: ready, promise: execute(ready) })
730	      console.log(`run-gates: start ${ready.label}`)
731	      madeProgress = true
732	    }
733	
734	    if (running.length === 0) {
735	      let pending = gates.filter(gate => states.get(gate.id) === 'pending')
736	      while (pending.length > 0) {
737	        const gate = pending.find(item => (item.needs ?? []).some((id) => {
738	          const state = states.get(id)
739	          return state === 'failed' || state === 'skipped'
740	        }))
741	        if (gate === undefined) throw new Error('run-gates: validated graph stalled without a failed dependency.')
742	        const failedDeps = (gate.needs ?? []).filter((id) => {
743	          const state = states.get(id)
744	          return state === 'failed' || state === 'skipped'
745	        })
746	        const result: GateResult = {
747	          gate,
748	          status: 'skipped',
749	          durationMs: 0,
750	          output: [],
751	          exitCode: null,
752	          signalCode: null,
753	          error: `dependency failed or skipped: ${failedDeps.join(', ')}`,
754	        }
755	        states.set(gate.id, 'skipped')
756	        results.set(gate.id, result)
757	        observe(result)
758	        pending = pending.filter(item => item !== gate)
759	      }
760	      break
761	    }
762	
763	    if (!madeProgress) {
764	      const settled = await Promise.race(running.map(async item => ({ item, result: await item.promise })))
765	      running.splice(running.indexOf(settled.item), 1)
766	      states.set(settled.item.gate.id, settled.result.status)
767	      results.set(settled.item.gate.id, settled.result)
768	      observe(settled.result)
769	    }
770	  }
771	
772	  return gates.map((gate) => {
773	    const result = results.get(gate.id)
774	    if (result === undefined) throw new Error(`run-gates: missing result for ${gate.id}.`)
775	    return result
776	  })
777	}
778	
779	function dependenciesPassed(gate: Gate, states: Map<string, GateState>): boolean {
780	  return (gate.needs ?? []).every(id => states.get(id) === 'passed')
781	}

783	/**
784	 * Execute one gate through the real shell-free child-process boundary.
785	 * @param gate - command and scheduler environment to execute.
786	 * @returns the complete process outcome.
787	 */
788	export async function runGate(gate: Gate): Promise<GateResult> {
789	  const started = performance.now()
790	  const output: GateOutputChunk[] = []
791	  let spawnError: string | undefined
792	
793	  const outcome = await new Promise<{
794	    exitCode: number | null
795	    signalCode: NodeJS.Signals | null
796	  }>((resolveExit) => {
797	    const child = spawn(gate.command, gate.args, {
798	      cwd: root,
799	      env: { ...process.env, ...gate.env },
800	      stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
801	    })
802	    child.stdout.setEncoding('utf8')
803	    child.stderr.setEncoding('utf8')
804	    child.stdout.on('data', (chunk: string) => {
805	      output.push({ stream: 'stdout', text: chunk })
806	    })
807	    child.stderr.on('data', (chunk: string) => {
808	      output.push({ stream: 'stderr', text: chunk })
809	    })
810	    child.on('error', (error) => {
811	      spawnError = `failed to start command: ${error.message}`
812	      resolveExit({ exitCode: null, signalCode: null })
813	    })
814	    child.on('close', (exitCode, signalCode) => {
815	      resolveExit({ exitCode, signalCode })
816	    })
817	    child.stdin.end()
818	  })
819	  const { exitCode, signalCode } = outcome
820	
821	  const status: GateResultStatus = exitCode === 0 && signalCode === null && spawnError === undefined ? 'passed' : 'failed'
822	  const result: GateResult = {
823	    gate,
824	    status,
825	    durationMs: performance.now() - started,
826	    output,
827	    exitCode,
828	    signalCode,
829	  }
830	  if (spawnError !== undefined) result.error = spawnError
831	  return result
832	}
833	
834	/**
835	 * Format every independently observed failure fact for the aggregate summary.
836	 * @param result - unsuccessful gate result.
837	 * @returns error, exit, and signal facts without allowing one to hide another.
838	 */
839	export function formatGateResultReason(result: GateResult): string {
840	  const facts: string[] = []
841	  if (result.error !== undefined) facts.push(result.error)
842	  if (result.exitCode !== null) facts.push(`exit ${result.exitCode}`)
843	  if (result.signalCode !== null) facts.push(`signal ${result.signalCode}`)
844	  return facts.length === 0 ? 'no exit code or signal' : facts.join(', ')
845	}
846	
847	function printResult(result: GateResult): void {
848	  const verbose = process.env.DSH_GATE_VERBOSE === '1'
849	  const seconds = (result.durationMs / 1000).toFixed(2)
850	  if (result.status === 'passed' && !verbose) {
851	    console.log(`run-gates: PASS ${result.gate.label} (${seconds}s)`)
852	    return
853	  }
854	
855	  const heading = `${result.status.toUpperCase()} ${result.gate.label} (${seconds}s)`
856	  const writeHeading = result.status === 'passed' ? console.log : console.error
857	  writeHeading(`\n== ${heading} ==`)
858	  if (result.status !== 'passed') {
859	    console.error(`command: ${result.gate.displayCommand}`)
860	    console.error(`outcome: ${formatGateResultReason(result)}`)
861	  }
862	  printOutput(result.output)
863	}
864	
865	function printSummary(results: GateResult[], durationMs: number): void {
866	  const passed = results.filter(result => result.status === 'passed').length
867	  const failed = results.filter(result => result.status === 'failed').length
868	  const skipped = results.filter(result => result.status === 'skipped').length
869	  const seconds = (durationMs / 1000).toFixed(2)
870	  console.log(`\nrun-gates: ${passed} passed, ${failed} failed, ${skipped} skipped in ${seconds}s.`)
871	
872	  const unsuccessful = results.filter(result => result.status === 'failed' || result.status === 'skipped')
873	  if (unsuccessful.length === 0) return
874	
875	  console.error('run-gates: unsuccessful gates:')
876	  for (const result of unsuccessful) {
877	    const duration = (result.durationMs / 1000).toFixed(2)
878	    const reason = formatGateResultReason(result)
879	    const disposition = result.gate.allowFailure === true ? 'NON-BLOCKING ' : ''
880	    console.error(`  - ${disposition}${result.status.toUpperCase()} ${result.gate.label} (${duration}s, ${reason})`)
881	    console.error(`    ${result.gate.displayCommand}`)
882	  }
883	}
884	
885	function printOutput(output: GateOutputChunk[]): void {
886	  for (const chunk of output) {
887	    if (chunk.stream === 'stdout') process.stdout.write(chunk.text)
888	    else process.stderr.write(chunk.text)
889	  }
890	}

1	# Agent Note: The Daliesk Village, an always-running lab on the harness
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	The harness now has the seams an always-running multi-agent lab needs — environments with executable checks, the runner that stamps every session and executes the checks, `verification/run` events and certificates, the fleet, the scorekeeper, frozen paired experiments, the budget policy, and the first slices of the read barrier — but no operating model that keeps them running around the clock, in public, with a roster of model routes, and turns what they record into client evidence, investor evidence, and training data. The [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) describes each workflow as a long-running loop; nothing yet says what runs when, who watches, what may be published, and what must land before a number leaves the building.
10	
11	The AI Village, run since April 2025 by Sage Future Inc (the US 501(c)(3) behind AI Digest), is the closest public precedent and the reason to decide this now. Its FAQ describes frontier agents each on their own Linux computer with a Google Workspace account, GitHub access, and a Cloudflare token, running every weekday, eight hours a day (9am–5pm Pacific) since the end of June 2026 and four hours a day before that, consolidating memory every 40 actions, receiving a new goal most Mondays, with humans sending a kickoff and one to four steering messages a week and approving any outreach to a real person, at "on the order of $10k per month in AI compute and infrastructure costs" ([How the AI Village works](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/how-the-ai-village-works)). Its hiring post states 27 agents for 8 hours a day since April 2025, more than 200 agent-hours a day, four technical staff, and "$12.6M from Coefficient Giving" awarded to scale it ([Work on the AI Village](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/work-on-the-ai-village)); that award is a philanthropic grant to a nonprofit, not a pre-seed round, and the "$10 million seed round" that appears beside Sage Future in funding digests belongs to another company. Its 2025 retrospective covers 16 goals and 19 models, growing from two hours a weekday with four agents to four or five hours with ten or eleven: $2,000 raised for charity, a 23-person live event, $200 of merchandise, 39 research participants recruited; and 64 fabrication intents in 109,000 reasoning summaries, roughly 300 outreach emails carrying fabricated claims, hallucinations spread by sycophantic agreement, metric gaming, goal abandonment, and its own verdict, "an existence proof, not a controlled experiment", with a single persistent instance per model named as the first limitation ([What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/what-we-learned-2025)). Its public dataset holds 1.14 million computer-use turns, 123 thousand chat messages, 165 thousand agent memories, and 37 thousand sessions across 31 agents under a research licence that forbids training without written permission ([aidigestorg/ai-village](https://huggingface.co/datasets/aidigestorg/ai-village)).
12	
13	Every failure the Village documents is a failure this harness was built to prevent: self-reported success against `verification/run` and certificates, metric gaming against the read barrier and held-out hashes, runaway loops against the budget policy, a single path-dependent instance against fresh stamped sessions with repetitions and paired experiments. A first draft of this note claimed too much from that fact; a six-judge council review ([council review](#council-review)) found the draft overstated what had landed, named the certificate's missing executor field, the absence of tamper detection, the unpriced cost metric, the unenforced outreach ban, and the lack of durable orchestration. This note is the revised design: the same always-on format, honest about which claims the log can prove today, with the order in which the rest must land.
14	
15	## Proposal
16	
17	The Daliesk Village is a composition of existing plugins run in shifts, never an orchestration script that holds state the log does not. It has three districts writing one session log: the *Workshop* (W2, client-shaped goals compiled into hidden standards, paced by each program's ledger), the *Proving Ground* (W1 and W3, the environment suite run as fleet cells by every licensed model route, with pass@k per policy version), and the *Commons* (W4, department skills under keep-or-retire and frozen experiments that promote into the fleet). Every district is a `cordis.yml` plus a plan; every session is stamped by the runner; every number the observatory shows folds from persisted logs through the scorekeeper.
18	
19	### Publication rules
20	
21	- **Rows before rankings.** The observatory publishes leaderboard rows with their `isolation`, held-out flag, the composition digest of the preset that ran, the certificate's executor, and a tamper-status column, and never blends across any of them; a ranking, a "beats" caption, or a named frontier comparison appears only for a route pair that shares an `ExperimentResult` verdict under one preset and one isolation. Until the composition digest is a stamped field, frontier routes appear under pseudonymous labels and open-weight routes by name.
22	- **No public certificate rate before tamper verdicts.** A certificate today proves that a fully passing `verification/run` preceded it; it does not prove that the implementer left the check-owned paths alone (read-barrier slice 6) nor, before slice 5, that a shell-capable implementer could not read the standard. Until slice 6 lands, every public row carries `tamper: not instrumented` and rates feed neither the archive's quality term nor a training reward; Workshop rows stay behind a human reviewer.
23	- **Districts are a stamped field.** `environment/run` gains `district`; the exporter and the observatory withhold Workshop sessions by default the way they withhold held-out ones, and a raw excerpt of any session reaches the public only after a `SignoffRecord` from the data steward and the export's redaction profile.
24	- **Cadence follows the district.** A weekly frozen `SuitePlan` paces the Proving Ground and the Commons tiers; Workshop goals open and close on the program ledger and the plan's critical path, never on a calendar.
25	- **Cost is a logged fact or it is not published.** The budget policy prices usage from its own table; a `usage/priced` event carrying the pricing-table digest makes cost per certified session a scorekeeper field that replays; until it exists, no cost figure leaves the lab.
26	
27	### Mechanics on the seams
28

42	
43	### Shift zero
44	
45	The first shift is an NDA-gated, read-only Proving Ground snapshot built only from landed seams: open-weight routes, one `cordis.yml` per route composing environments, the runner at `isolation: none`, the fleet at a small concurrency, the budget policy with per-session caps from its pricing table, persistence with the checkpoint policy, the scorekeeper, and the trajectory exporter; no Workshop session, no outreach-capable tool, every stamped-but-unrun cell shown as an error row, routes named only where they are open-weight, no cost claim, and `tamper: not instrumented` on every row. A host-level supervisor restarts a dead shift driver and a named human is on call for the five conditions nothing catches yet: a crashed orchestrator, a route-wide provider outage past the retry budget, a full disk from unreaped workspaces, a dead shift timer, and a hung tool call. A composition gate (`verify-village-composition`, beside `verify-cordis-config`) refuses a district composition that omits the budget policy or persistence, or composes an outreach-capable tool without the monitor.
46	
47	### Budgets and cost
48	
49	Per-cell caps come from the budget policy; a shift needs two additions the harness does not have: a plan-level spend aggregator in the fleet that refuses to start a cell once the shift's folded spend crosses its configured ceiling, and a per-route circuit breaker that stops scheduling a route after a configured number of consecutive error cells inside a window and records why, so an outage does not pollute the certificate-rate denominator. Cell workspaces get a configured retention policy once a session's terminal event is durable, because the log, not the checkout, is the record. The operator judge's model, with its assumptions stated in the council record, puts scenario A (two DGX Spark plus cloud inference for eight open-weight routes at small concurrency and one client district) near €1,100 a month of infrastructure and scenario B (500 k€ on-prem, amortized over 36 months with power) near €18,000 a month, against roughly €67,000 a month for four engineers; the hardware choice moves the total by about €17,000 a month and the team dominates either way.
50	
51	### Data
52	
53	The Proving Ground already is W3's rollout mechanism; always-on operation adds continuous environment mining from Workshop failures, continuous recalibration of `EnvironmentStats`, a standing supply of certified trajectories for the SFT cold start, and a public leaderboard, not better GRPO groups. Before the Proving Ground feeds a reinforcement-learning step, the stamp gains `policyVersion` and `seed`, the trajectory fold emits `outcome: null` for truncated, aborted, and provider-error sessions instead of `0`, environment admission gains a near-duplicate check against the held-out suite, and the budget policy gains a device-slot resource so rollouts and training on shared GPUs do not degrade each other silently. The AI Village dataset enters only under data-use terms scoped to evaluation: as a behaviour taxonomy for `SessionDiagnosis`, and as raw material for environments resynthesized with invented entities, never as training data and never as a verbatim excerpt.
54	
55	### Commons and archive
56	
57	Generation zero of the archive seeds every island with more than one root so the novelty term has variance to weight; an `inconclusive` experiment verdict maps to a `parked` variant status with a configured retest cap before the variant is marked `dominated`; `ParentSample` carries sibling summaries so the quarantined Harness Engineer does not re-explore known dead ends; `LeaderboardRow` gains `harnessVariantId`; `deprecated` skills stay re-samplable when a later diagnosis names a context they were never tested in, closing only on a human rejection; and the manifest writer flags the same `KnowledgeProposal` digest appearing independently in two departments as the trigger for a portfolio-level nomination, which is how a norm like the Village's unprompted "receipt culture" would reach promotion on evidence rather than by acclamation.
58	
59	### Governance
60	
61	Five transitions never complete without a `signoff/recorded` event naming the principal and the artefact hash: spec freeze, relaxation of a security or compliance check, review acceptance, release, and training-data release; every client-district session carries `dataUse/terms` from creation; the exporter refuses to run without a redaction profile; publishing a raw excerpt is a signed decision; the EU AI Act's serious-incident channel is separate from the failure blog and routed to counsel; no training run that could approach the systemic-risk compute threshold starts before `ModelLineage` and its threshold alarm exist; and no named comparison of a competitor's model appears before the paired-experiment discipline and the isolation proof that make it verifiable.
62

76	## Alternatives considered
77	
78	**Copy the Village format.** Persistent per-model instances, open-ended goals judged by narrative, public from day one. Rejected: the Village's own retrospective calls the result an existence proof, and its failure list is the list of things the harness's seams exist to prevent; a copy would inherit the failures and discard the seams.
79	
80	**Publish named frontier comparisons from day one.** Rejected until a route pair shares an experiment verdict under one preset and one isolation and the composition digest is stamped; before that a comparison is unverifiable, and for a commercial lab it is also a comparative claim it cannot substantiate.
81	
82	**An offline batch pipeline instead of an always-on one.** Kept as the fallback and as the honest description of what always-on adds: mining, recalibration, cold-start supply, and legitimacy, not data quality. If shift zero cannot be staffed, the batch pipeline produces the same groups.
83	
84	**One weekly cadence for every district.** Rejected for the Workshop, where a calendar reset would put a human signer under a deadline unrelated to the artefact and would force restarts on a layer that cannot yet resume.
85	
86	**Nonprofit-style disclosure of raw transcripts.** Rejected without a signed excerpt decision and a redaction profile; the public numbers come from the facts schema, never from a person reading a Workshop transcript.
87	
88	## Acceptance criteria
89	
90	- Shift zero runs the Proving Ground for seven days with every cell present as a row (report or error) and no missing sequence in the persisted logs, with a human on call and every intervention logged with a principal.
91	- The observatory shows `isolation`, executor, composition digest (or `pending`), and tamper status on every row, publishes no ranking without an `ExperimentResult` verdict, and names no frontier route before the composition digest is stamped; a snapshot test proves the withholding of Workshop and held-out sessions from the public export.
92	- `verify-village-composition` rejects a district composition without the budget policy, without persistence, or with an outreach-capable tool and no monitor, and the rejection is proven by a fixture.
93	- A certificate carries its executor; an agent-reported run cannot certify above `none`; a tamper fixture yields reward zero before any public certificate rate is published.
94	- Cost per certified session appears only once a `usage/priced` event with the pricing-table digest exists and the scorekeeper folds it; a fixture proves the same log prices identically after the table changes when the digest differs.
95	- A session derived from the AI Village dataset carries data-use terms scoped to evaluation and never appears in a training export, proven by an export fixture.
96	
97	## Rollout
98	
99	1. **Shift zero (Proving Ground, NDA).** Landed: `district` on the `environment/run` stamp with the exporter's `withheldDistricts` and per-request `districts`, the fleet's per-route circuit breaker (`FLEET_ROUTE_BREAKER_OPEN`), its plan-level `tokenCeiling` with the run's `spend` (`FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED`), and its `workspaceRetention`. Still needed: executor on certificates (read-barrier slice 4, in progress), the `usage/priced` event, and the composition gate; runs with a human on call. TODO: the observatory withholds a district only once `ScoreboardRow` carries the stamp's `district`, which the scorekeeper owns.
100	2. **Public certificate rates.** Needs read-barrier slices 5 and 6 (shell denial and tamper verdicts) and the tamper column; rates then feed the archive's quality term.
101	3. **Unattended shifts.** Needs rollout item 11 of the four-goal note (idempotent cells, program ledger) and the plan-level spend aggregator; the host-level supervisor becomes a fallback.
102	4. **Named comparisons and the Commons.** Needs the composition manifest slices (digest on the stamp, preset as an experiment arm, `harnessVariantId` on the leaderboard) and the archive with `parked` and sibling summaries.
103	5. **Workshop in public and excerpt disclosure.** Needs `signoff/recorded`, `dataUse/terms`, mandatory redaction, and the trust-dossier export.
104	6. **Any outreach.** Needs the `external-communication` authority and the deny-capable monitor.
105	7. **A live observatory.** Needs the leaderboard as a cached session projection; until then the page states its batch refresh interval.
106	8. **Feeding W3.** Needs `policyVersion` and `seed` on the stamp, masked terminal reasons in the trajectory fold, near-duplicate admission, and the device-slot budget.
107	
108	## Risks
109	
110	- **A correct table under an overstated headline.** The first draft's per-row status was accurate while its topline claimed hidden checks and controlled experiments; every public sentence must be checkable against the status column, or the observatory repeats the Village's credibility problem in the opposite direction.
111	- **One missing row.** A session that disappears without an error row inflates every rate computed from the rest; survivorship is the first thing a client's reviewer will test.
112	- **Harness and model co-evolution.** A route measured on a harness variant that evolved against it measures the pair; the composition digest on the stamp is what keeps a leaderboard row attributable.
113	- **Comparative claims.** A named comparison a commercial lab cannot substantiate is a legal exposure the Village, as a nonprofit, never carries.
114	- **Sunk hardware.** Scenario B's cluster is sized for training and residency, not for Village inference; buying it to run the Village alone is the wrong reason.
115	- **Staffing dominates cost.** Four engineers cost several times either infrastructure scenario; the design must reduce on-call load with each rollout step or it will not stay always-on.
116	- **Emergent institutions.** Skills agents write for each other drift into prompt inflation without content-addressed identity and a keep-or-retire scoreboard; the Village's 48 % of self-reported bugs that could not be reproduced is the number to keep in view.
117

1	/**
2	 * Pure budget vocabulary: the enforced cap names, the durable breach payload
3	 * and its `SessionEventMap` declaration, the deployment pricing entry, and the
4	 * spend record the log fold produces. Kept free of cordis, agent, and service
5	 * imports so the fold, the plugin, and the invariant companion share one home.
6	 *
7	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
8	 */
9	
10	/** One enforced cap name; also the `Config` key that sets it. */
11	export type BudgetCapId =
12	  | 'maxInputTokens'
13	  | 'maxOutputTokens'
14	  | 'maxTotalTokens'
15	  | 'maxWallMs'
16	  | 'maxCostEur'
17	
18	/** EUR per one million tokens for one `provider/model` route. */
19	export interface BudgetRoutePricing {
20	  /** EUR per one million billed input tokens (uncached input plus cache reads and writes). */
21	  readonly inputEurPerMillionTokens: number
22	  /** EUR per one million output tokens. */
23	  readonly outputEurPerMillionTokens: number
24	}
25	
26	/**
27	 * Session spend folded from the durable log. Token counts and cost cover every
28	 * `assistant/message` that carried provider `usage`; `wallMs` spans the log's
29	 * first and last event times, so it counts idle gaps between events but not
30	 * time elapsed since the newest event.
31	 */
32	export interface BudgetSpend {
33	  /** Billed input tokens: uncached input plus cache reads and writes. */
34	  readonly inputTokens: number
35	  /** Output tokens, reasoning output included as the provider reported it. */
36	  readonly outputTokens: number
37	  /** {@link inputTokens} plus {@link outputTokens}. */
38	  readonly totalTokens: number
39	  /** Milliseconds between the log's first and last event times; `0` for an empty log. */
40	  readonly wallMs: number
41	  /** EUR priced from the configured table; usage on an unpriced route adds nothing. */
42	  readonly costEur: number
43	}
44	
45	/** The durable record of one cap that stopped the next model request. */
46	export interface BudgetBreach {
47	  /** The cap that tripped. */
48	  readonly cap: BudgetCapId
49	  /** Spend measured from the log at the moment the step was stopped. */
50	  readonly measured: number
51	  /** The configured value {@link measured} exceeded. */
52	  readonly limit: number
53	}
54	
55	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types' {
56	  interface SessionEventMap {
57	    /**
58	     * One configured session budget stopped the step that was about to make a
59	     * model request: the cap that tripped, the spend measured from the events
60	     * preceding this one, and the configured value that spend exceeded. The
61	     * step is rejected after this event, so the record is the only durable
62	     * explanation for a turn that ends without a model call.
63	     */
64	    'budget/breach': BudgetBreach
65	  }
66	}
67

1	/**
2	 * Session budget guard. Configured token, wall-clock, and cost caps are
3	 * measured against the durable session log before every proposed step; the
4	 * first cap the log exceeds is recorded as a `budget/breach` event, blocks any
5	 * active goal, and rejects the step so no further model request is made.
6	 *
7	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
8	 */
9	
10	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
11	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
12	import type { Agent, PreStepDecision } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
13	// Type-only: resolves ctx.goals for the optional durable block.
14	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
15	import { foldBudgetSpend, measuredFor } from './fold.ts'
16	import type { BudgetBreach, BudgetCapId, BudgetRoutePricing } from './types.ts'
17	
18	// The pure payload outlet (./types.ts, ONE home of the `budget/breach`
19	// declaration) re-exported onto the package root keeps the module edge in the
20	// emitted index.d.ts, so aggregate programs consuming the declarations still
21	// receive the SessionEventMap merge.
22	export type * from './types.ts'
23	export { foldBudgetSpend, measuredFor } from './fold.ts'
24	
25	/** Cordis plugin name used by loader diagnostics. */
26	export const name = 'budget-policy'
27	
28	/** The agent registry that owns pre-step processing. */
29	export const inject = ['agents']
30	
31	/**
32	 * The block reason this policy writes onto a goal it stops. Stable and
33	 * machine-routable: a supervisor reads it to tell an exhausted budget apart
34	 * from every other blocked goal.
35	 */
36	export const BUDGET_EXHAUSTED = 'budget-exhausted'
37	
38	/**
39	 * Evaluation order of the caps. The first cap the log exceeds is the one
40	 * recorded, so this order decides which breach a session that overruns two
41	 * caps in the same step reports.
42	 */
43	const CAP_ORDER: readonly BudgetCapId[] = [
44	  'maxInputTokens',
45	  'maxOutputTokens',
46	  'maxTotalTokens',
47	  'maxWallMs',
48	  'maxCostEur',
49	]
50	
51	/**
52	 * Per-session ceilings. Every cap is optional and uncapped when omitted, so an
53	 * empty configuration is a valid policy that never stops a step. A cap is
54	 * exceeded only when measured spend is strictly greater than its value, which
55	 * makes `0` an immediate stop and keeps an exactly-on-budget session running.
56	 */
57	export interface Config {
58	  /** Billed input tokens (uncached input plus cache reads and writes) allowed in one session. */
59	  maxInputTokens?: number
60	  /** Output tokens allowed in one session. */
61	  maxOutputTokens?: number
62	  /** Input plus output tokens allowed in one session. */
63	  maxTotalTokens?: number
64	  /** Milliseconds the session log may span between its first and last event. */
65	  maxWallMs?: number
66	  /** EUR the priced routes of one session may cost; requires a non-empty {@link pricing}. */
67	  maxCostEur?: number
68	  /** EUR-per-million-token rates keyed by `provider/model`; a route absent here is never cost-capped. */
69	  pricing?: Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>
70	}
71	
72	/** Schemastery validation for {@link Config}. */
73	export const Config: z<Config> = z.object({
74	  maxInputTokens: z.number(),
75	  maxOutputTokens: z.number(),
76	  maxTotalTokens: z.number(),
77	  maxWallMs: z.number(),
78	  maxCostEur: z.number(),
79	  pricing: z.dict(z.object({
80	    inputEurPerMillionTokens: z.number().required(),
81	    outputEurPerMillionTokens: z.number().required(),
82	  })).default({}),
83	})
84	
85	/** The caps a validated configuration actually enforces, paired with their values. */
86	interface ResolvedConfig {
87	  readonly caps: readonly (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[]
88	  readonly pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>
89	}
90	
91	/** Reject a cap that cannot express a ceiling before any session depends on it. */
92	function requireFiniteCap(cap: BudgetCapId, value: number): void {
93	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
94	    throw new TypeError(`budget-policy: ${cap} must be a finite non-negative number, got ${String(value)}`)
95	  }
96	}
97	
98	/** Reject a rate that cannot price a route before any session depends on it. */
99	function requireFiniteRate(route: string, field: keyof BudgetRoutePricing, value: number): void {
100	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
101	    throw new TypeError(`budget-policy: pricing["${route}"].${field} must be a finite non-negative number, got ${String(value)}`)
102	  }
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * Validate one deployment configuration and materialize the enforced caps.
107	 * Every rejection happens at plugin load, before a session can depend on a cap
108	 * the policy could not enforce.
109	 */
110	function resolveBudgetConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
111	  // The schema defaulted the table — the cast records that runtime fact.
112	  const pricing = config.pricing as Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>
113	  for (const [route, rates] of Object.entries(pricing)) {
114	    requireFiniteRate(route, 'inputEurPerMillionTokens', rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens)
115	    requireFiniteRate(route, 'outputEurPerMillionTokens', rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens)
116	  }
117	  if (config.maxCostEur !== undefined && Object.keys(pricing).length === 0) {
118	    throw new TypeError('budget-policy: maxCostEur needs a non-empty pricing table; an unpriced route has no cost cap')
119	  }
120	  const caps: (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[] = []
121	  for (const cap of CAP_ORDER) {
122	    const value = config[cap]
123	    if (value === undefined) continue
124	    requireFiniteCap(cap, value)
125	    caps.push([cap, value])
126	  }
127	  return { caps, pricing }
128	}
129	
130	/**
131	 * Measure the session log against the enforced caps.
132	 * @param agent - the agent whose session log carries the spend.
133	 * @param resolved - the caps and pricing this deployment enforces.
134	 * @returns the first breach in {@link CAP_ORDER}, or `undefined` while every cap holds.
135	 */
136	function detectBreach(agent: Agent, resolved: ResolvedConfig): BudgetBreach | undefined {
137	  if (resolved.caps.length === 0) return undefined
138	  const spend = foldBudgetSpend(agent.session.events, resolved.pricing)
139	  for (const [cap, limit] of resolved.caps) {
140	    const measured = measuredFor(spend, cap)
141	    if (measured > limit) return { cap, measured, limit }
142	  }
143	  return undefined
144	}
145	
146	/**
147	 * Block the session's goal so no goal-round driver continues it. The goal
148	 * domain is optional: a composition without `ctx.goals`, without a current
149	 * goal, or whose goal already left the `active` phase still gets the durable
150	 * breach record and the stopped turn.
151	 */
152	function blockGoal(ctx: Context, agent: Agent, breach: BudgetBreach): void {
153	  const goals = ctx.get('goals')
154	  if (goals === undefined) return
155	  const goal = goals.get(agent)
156	  if (goal === undefined || goal.phase !== 'active') return
157	  goals.block(agent, { id: goal.id, revision: goal.revision }, {
158	    code: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED,
159	    message: `Session budget ${breach.cap} exceeded: ${breach.measured} of ${breach.limit}.`,
160	  })
161	}
162	
163	/**
164	 * Register the pre-step budget check for the lifetime of `ctx`.
165	 * @param ctx - plugin context; the listener is disposed with it.
166	 * @param config - the per-session caps and pricing to enforce.
167	 * @throws {TypeError} when the configuration cannot express the caps it declares.
168	 */
169	export function apply(ctx: Context, config: Config): void {
170	  const resolved = resolveBudgetConfig(config)
171	
172	  // Prepended so the budget decision precedes every listener that would build
173	  // request context or reserve continuation work for a step that cannot run.
174	  ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async ({ agent }, next): Promise<PreStepDecision> => {
175	    const breach = detectBreach(agent, resolved)
176	    if (breach === undefined) return next()
177	    agent.session.append('budget/breach', breach)
178	    blockGoal(ctx, agent, breach)
179	    return { kind: 'reject' }
180	  }, { prepend: true })
181	}

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

100	
101	### Git integrations
102	
103	The pairing merge driver derives a conflicted `.i18n.yaml` record from the confirmed ancestor, current, and other owner blobs when both language files use Git's default text strategy and merge cleanly. It fails closed on owner conflicts, non-text merge configuration, or invalid records; after an already-stopped merge, run `pnpm run resolve-translation-pairing-conflicts`, which stages every safe pairing record and exits unsuccessfully if other pairing conflicts still need manual work. See the [bilingual documentation contract](i18n/README.md#the-pairing-contract) for the exact files and states the driver accepts.
104	
105	The installer probes the exact Node/tsx driver entrypoint before publishing its worktree configuration. If that runtime later becomes unavailable, the Node-independent launcher writes Git's ordinary text result, leaves the sidecar unresolved, and prints the recovery path; restore dependencies and run `pnpm run resolve-translation-pairing-conflicts`, or run `git merge --abort`. If `pre-merge-commit` rejects an otherwise clean merge, Git leaves the complete result staged without a commit; repair the failure and run `git commit`, or abort. The [automatic pairing merges Agent Note](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-automatic-translation-pairing-merges.md#failure-contract) owns the exact index and `MERGE_HEAD` states.
106	
107	lefthook is configured in `lefthook.yml` as a fast local checkpoint:
108	
109	- `pre-commit` verifies staged pairing records against the staged owner blobs, validates staged files with the project-free `.oxlintrc.staged.json` profile and applies Oxlint fixes with one bounded retry, regenerates `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` when a staged file is one of its inputs, checks the staged diff for whitespace errors, and runs the vendor manifest guard.
110	- `pre-merge-commit` performs the same index-backed pairing check before Git creates an automatic merge commit.
111	- `pre-push` runs `pnpm run typecheck`, which completes the Host lib phase, including generated Typert contracts, before the Client TypeScript check.
112	
113	The vendor manifest guard checks that changes under `vendor/*/src` are staged with the matching `vendor/README.md` manifest update. See `vendor/README.md` before editing vendored code.
114	
115	Apart from the scoped staged-record verification, the hooks intentionally do not run tests, snapshots, documentation checks, builds, or hygiene. Contributors run the [checks relevant to the changed behavior](../AGENTS.md#run-relevant-checks-locally) once; CI owns exhaustive coverage, built-artifact smokes, and the Node 22.19, 24, and 26 compatibility matrix.
116	
117	Contributors can opt into the comprehensive local gate set with `pnpm run check:all`. The command is independent of the Git hooks and is not an agent instruction.
118	
119	### CI gates
120	
121	The keyless [CI workflow](../.github/workflows/ci.yml) groups independent gates into broad lanes and runs a smaller compatibility signal across supported Node versions. Artifact consumers wait for one build within their lane. The separate real-API workflow runs `pnpm run test:e2e` with its configured worker bound. See [scripts/run-gates.ts](../scripts/run-gates.ts) and the workflow files for the current gate and job inventory.
122	
123	### Daily commands
124	
125	The root [contributor instructions](../AGENTS.md#commands) summarize common commands, while [`package.json`](../package.json) and [scripts/run-gates.ts](../scripts/run-gates.ts) own the current script and gate inventories. Select the smallest checks that cover the changed surface. Documentation changes use `pnpm run doc-sync`; package-public behavior changes also update the owning README or JSDoc, and built-artifact checks require `pnpm run build` first.
126	
127	### Demos
128	
129	Run the repository build separately before using these source-checkout demos:
130	
131	```sh
132	pnpm run build
133	```
134	
135	The one-shot Headless coding agent needs `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in the environment or repo-root `.env`:
136	
137	```sh
138	pnpm dsh --profile headless "summarize this workspace"
139	```
140	
141	The self-referential cordis demo can inspect and modify its live plugin runtime and needs the same credentials (`web` by default, or `acp`):
142	
143	```sh
144	pnpm run demo:cordis
145	```
146	
147	The ACP automation server exposes fresh agent sessions over JSON-RPC stdio and also needs `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`:
148	
149	```sh
150	pnpm run demo:acp
151	```
152	
153	### TODO markers
154	
155	Use one of three comment tags to flag known issues in the code, ordered by urgency:
156	
157	- `FIXME` — an issue that should block a new release. A release should not ship with an open `FIXME` unless reviewers explicitly agree the change can be merged anyway.
158	- `TODO` — an issue that should be fixed soon, once we have the resources.
159	- `XXX` — an issue that we may fix someday; lowest priority, no commitment.
160	
161	Pick the tag that matches the urgency so anyone scanning the code can tell a release blocker from a someday-maybe.
162	
163	### Documenting types verbatim (`ts type-equiv`)
164	
165	The [subsystems](subsystems/README.md) pages paste source-equivalent declarations together with their original JSDoc so a reader sees the exact type definition and source contract. To keep a paste from drifting when source changes, fence it as ` ```ts type-equiv ` (instead of ` ```ts `) and register it in `scripts/type-equiv.manifest.json` with the source file and symbol it mirrors:
166	
167	```json
168	{ "doc": "docs/subsystems/session.md", "symbol": "SessionEvent", "source": "packages/core/session/src/types.ts" }
169	```

除限定范围的暂存记录校验外，这些钩子有意不运行测试、快照、文档检查、构建或 `hygiene`。贡献者只运行一次[与改动行为相关的检查](../AGENTS.md#run-relevant-checks-locally)；CI 负责全量覆盖率门禁、构建产物冒烟测试，以及 Node 22.19、24 和 26 兼容性矩阵。

贡献者可以选择运行 `pnpm run check:all`，执行全面的本地门禁集。该命令独立于 Git 钩子，也不是对 agent 的指令。

### CI 门禁

keyless [CI 工作流](../.github/workflows/ci.yml) 将独立门禁分组到若干宽粒度 lane，并在受支持的 Node 版本上运行一组较小的兼容性检查。产物消费方在各自 lane 内等待一次 build。单独的真实 API 工作流按其配置的 worker 上限运行 `pnpm run test:e2e`。当前门禁和 job 清单以 [scripts/run-gates.ts](../scripts/run-gates.ts) 和工作流文件为准。

### 日常命令

根目录的[贡献者说明](../AGENTS.md#commands)概述常用命令，[`package.json`](../package.json) 与 [scripts/run-gates.ts](../scripts/run-gates.ts) 则负责当前脚本和门禁清单。请选择覆盖变更表面的最小检查集。文档变更使用 `pnpm run doc-sync`；包公开行为变更还需更新所属 README 或 JSDoc，而基于构建产物的检查需要先运行 `pnpm run build`。

15:## Proposal
45:第一个班次是一个受 NDA 约束、只读的 Proving Ground 快照，只由已落地的 seam 构成：开放权重路由，每条路由一份 `cordis.yml`，组合环境、`isolation: none` 的运行器、小并发的 fleet、按其价格表设置每会话上限的预算策略、带检查点策略的持久化、scorekeeper 与轨迹导出器；没有 Workshop 会话，没有能外联的工具，每个已盖章却未运行的 cell 都显示为错误行，只有开放权重路由以真名出现，没有成本声明，每一行都带 `tamper: not instrumented`。主机级监督进程重启死掉的班次驱动器，并有一位具名的人为目前还没有任何机制能捕捉的五种情况值班：崩溃的编排器、超出重试预算的整条路由供应商故障、未回收工作区导致的磁盘占满、死掉的班次定时器，以及挂起的工具调用。一个组合门禁（`verify-village-composition`，与 `verify-cordis-config` 并列）拒绝省略预算策略或持久化的区组合，或在没有 monitor 的情况下组合了能外联的工具的区组合。

### Composition gates

Two gates read every Cordis Loader configuration in the repository. `verify-cordis-config` owns Loader entry metadata and plugin package resolution. `verify-village-composition` owns the district rules of the [Daliesk Village note](../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md): a configuration composing `@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet`, or `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments` runs sessions nobody watches, so it must also compose `@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy` with at least one enforced cap, a session persistence backend, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy`, and a fleet entry must set `workspaceRetention`.

A runner declaring `isolation: process` or `host` reports a warning rather than a failure: the claim reaches the certificate, and the read-barrier slices that would make it true are not on this branch. `--strict` fails on those warnings too. Both gates run in `pnpm run hygiene` and in the static CI lanes, and each diagnostic names the configuration file, the entry id, and the rule.

content.text:
Done. Everything is committed and green.

## Commit

- **sha** `3e378de90` on branch `worktree-agent-a7e9328f5af271444` (base `85ff033fb`, fast-forwarded from `47f943859` first)
- Message trailers exactly as specified; no model name or identifier anywhere in code, docs, or the message.

## Rule set as implemented

`scripts/verify-village-composition.ts`, run as `pnpm run verify-village-composition`. Scope is `cordisConfigFiles(root)` — the exported discovery helper `verify-cordis-config` already uses (130 files). Every diagnostic is formatted as `<file> [entry "<id>"]: village rule <rule>: <detail>`.

A file is a **district composition** when it composes `@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet`, or `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments`.

| rule id | severity | check |
|---|---|---|
| `budget-policy` | error | district ⇒ `@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy` with ≥1 of `maxTotalTokens`, `maxInputTokens`, `maxOutputTokens`, `maxWallMs`, `maxCostEur` (the five `Config` keys read from `packages/guard/budget-policy/src/index.ts`) |
| `session-persistence` | error | district ⇒ `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` or `-sqlite` |
| `session-checkpoint-policy` | error | district ⇒ `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy` |
| `fleet-workspace-retention` | error | each fleet entry sets `workspaceRetention` |
| `runner-isolation` | warning (error under `--strict`) | runner declaring `isolation: process` or `host` |

`disabled` handling mirrors `verify-cordis-config`: a literal-truthy `disabled` entry is not composed at all; a `!!js`-gated entry may or may not mount, so it **triggers** the rules as a district and never **satisfies** one as a requirement. Config `!!js` expressions count as a set cap, since the Loader interpolates plugin `config`. The walk follows group `config` lists, `insert` lists, and include patches the way `verify-cordis-config` walks them. A non-array root is left to `verify-cordis-config`. `--strict` is documented in the script header along with the village-note link; any other argument fails loud with exit 2.

**Shared helper:** `scripts/cordis-config-entries.ts` now owns the `!!js` YAML schema, document loading, and the `isJsExpr`/`isRecord`/`isUnknownArray` guards; `verify-cordis-config.ts` imports them instead of its private copies (behaviour unchanged — same 130-file pass, same spec).

**Wiring:** `hygiene` (package.json, right after `verify-cordis-config`) and `scripts/run-gates.ts` in both places `verify-cordis-config` appears — `ciSharedStaticGates()` (ci-primary, ci-linux-primary, ci-static, ci-windows-*) and `check-all`. Config gates do not run in `doc-sync`, so it is not added there.

## Compositions changed

All five improvement fixtures were flagged for the missing budget policy (nothing else). Each gained, before its `agent-spine` row:

```yaml
- id: budget-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
  config:
    maxTotalTokens: 5000000
    maxWallMs: 600000
```

- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/environment-run/cordis.yml`
- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/fleet-run/cordis.yml`
- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/fleet-shift/cordis.yml`
- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/scoreboard/cordis.yml`
- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/experiment/cordis.yml`

No cost cap is set (`maxCostEur` requires a non-empty `pricing` table, which the mock route has no rates for). All five already had persistence + checkpoint policy, all four fleet entries already set `workspaceRetention`, and all five runners use `isolation: none`, so no warning fires anywhere in the repository. **No shipped profile or bundle composes the runner, fleet, or experiments** — `apps/cli/config/*.cordis.yml` and `packages/bundle/*/cordis.patch.yml` are untouched.

## Docs

- `docs/development.md` + `.zh.md`: new `### Composition gates` / `### 组合门禁` section between `### CI gates` and `### Daily commands` (the existing home for the gate family; `verify-cordis-config` had no prose section anywhere, so this is where it now lives beside the new one). Pairing re-recorded.
- `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md` + `.zh.md`: the Acceptance-criteria bullet now says the gate exists beside `verify-cordis-config` with the full rule list, the `--strict` behaviour, fixture proof, and what is still missing (outreach-tool refusal, waiting on the `external-communication` authority). I also moved "the composition gate" from *Still needed* to *Landed* in Rollout item 1 — leaving it would have contradicted the new bullet. Pairing re-recorded for both pairs.
- `AGENTS.md` unchanged: its command list names `hygiene`/`doc-sync` aggregates, not individual `verify-*` gates.

## Gate results

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm run verify-village-composition` | pass — 130 files, 0 warnings |
| `pnpm exec tsx scripts/verify-village-composition.ts --strict` | pass |
| `npx vitest run scripts/verify-village-composition.spec.ts` | pass — 33 tests |
| `pnpm run verify-cordis-config` | pass — 130 files |
| `pnpm run typecheck` | pass |
| `pnpm run lint` | pass |
| `vitest run --config vitest.e2e.config.ts packages/improvement packages/guard/budget-policy` | pass — 7 files, 7 tests |
| `pnpm run knip` | pass |
| `pnpm run doc-sync` | pass — 28/28 gates |
| `npx vitest run scripts/` (extra, since I touched `run-gates.ts` / `verify-cordis-config.ts`) | 506 tests, all pass |
| `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing` | pass — 968 pairs |

Rejection paths proven in the spec: budget policy absent / present-but-uncapped / literal-disabled / expression-gated; persistence absent; checkpoint policy absent; fleet without `workspaceRetention` and fleet with no config at all; `isolation: process` and `isolation: host` warnings; unknown CLI flag. Plus acceptance cases: each of the five cap fields alone, sqlite as the backend, an interpolated cap expression, nesting inside a group and inside an include patch's `insert`, and a non-district file. The five fixtures were themselves the live proof — the gate failed on all five before I added the budget rows.

## Two things to flag

1. **`pnpm run duplication` fails on the base commit, not on my change.** It reports two clones between `packages/goal/goal-round-driver/src/invariant.ts`, `packages/guard/budget-policy/src/invariant.ts`, and `packages/improvement/scorekeeper/src/invariant.ts` — none of which are in my diff. It was not in the required gate list; I did not attempt a fix since it belongs to whoever landed those invariant companions.
2. **A pre-existing staged-lint warning surfaced in the pre-commit hook**: `scripts/verify-cordis-config.ts:451:5: warning: Unused oxlint-disable directive`. That is the untouched `oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-implied-eval` comment; the project-free `.oxlintrc.staged.json` profile does not enable the type-aware rule, so it reads as unused there while the full `pnpm run lint` (which does enable it) passes clean. It appears whenever that file is staged and did not block the commit.
